Equipment.Presenting: Desktop computer running the jsPsych experiment in a browser (exact machine/OS/browser version not reported)
Equipment.Monitor: 23.8-inch monitor, 1080 x 768, 60 Hz (as reported in the manuscript; note that 5 of the 60 raw exports show a narrower canvas width of 1440-1536 px instead of 1920 px, and that the reported physical values are self-consistent only for a 1920 px wide display - see detail)

Physical_Environment.Viewing_distance: 60 cm (chin rest; as reported in the manuscript)

Experimental_Design.Conditions: Matching task: 8 within-subject conditions (2 association: self vs other x 2 matchness: matching vs nonmatching x 2 difficulty: easy vs hard). Choice task: 8 within-subject conditions (2 association x 2 difficulty x 2 task relevance: relevant vs irrelevant). Between-subjects counterbalancing variable: the dimension associated with the identity (motion, n = 30, vs colour, n = 30)

Block_Structure.Block_number: Matching task: 4 blocks of 48 trials (8 conditions x 6 trials per block). Choice task: two relevance blocks (relevant, irrelevant; order counterbalanced), each organised in rest-delimited blocks of 32 trials (4 conditions x 8 trials) and/or 16 trials (4 conditions x 4 trials); participants completed 3-5 such blocks per relevance condition depending on the sequential-stopping outcome. Adaptive staircase: 8 groups of 12 trials (4 groups per dimension)
Block_Structure.Trial_number: Matching task: 192 trials per participant (8 conditions x 24; 4 blocks x 48). Choice task: 256 trials planned (8 conditions x 32), but the number completed varied between participants (192-288; median 256) because the number of trials was determined by a Bayesian sequential stopping rule (BF10 >= 10 or <= 0.1, maximum 60 participants); the manuscript's statement that the matching task also comprised 256 trials (32 per condition) does not match the raw exports - see detail (registered issue)
Block_Structure.Practice_trials: Matching task: 32 trials per round; choice task: 16 trials per round; rounds repeat until >=65% correct (1-12 rounds observed), so practice trial counts vary between participants

Trial_Structure.Fixation_duration: 500 ms (white '+' in 48 px font on a black background)
Trial_Structure.SOA: 0 ms (the dot field and the identity label are presented simultaneously within the same trial; the label appears below the dot field)
Trial_Structure.ISI: Approximately 0 ms (the stimulus starts immediately after the 500 ms fixation trial; not reported separately in the manuscript)
Trial_Structure.Response_deadline: 3000 ms (raw trial_duration, identical for all trials; not stated in the manuscript)
Trial_Structure.ITI: 300-1000 ms random (jsPsych default_iti), followed by the 500 ms fixation cross that opens the next trial
Trial_Structure.Feedback_duration: 500 ms (practice phase only: correct / incorrect / too fast (< 250 ms) / too slow (no response))

Stimulus_Properties.Fixation: White '+' (48 px font) on a black background, 500 ms
Stimulus_Properties.Shape: Random-dot kinematogram (RDK) carrying both a motion direction and a colour distribution: 100 dots, dot diameter 0.15 deg, moving within an invisible 8 deg diameter aperture at 3 deg/s, unlimited dot life. The identity-bearing stimulus layer is the feature of the associated dimension - motion direction (left/right) for motion-associated participants, dominant colour (blue/red) for colour-associated participants - and not a geometric shape; the other feature was also present and served as the target in the task-irrelevant block
Stimulus_Properties.Label: Identity label presented as an image: 我 (self) or 他 / 她 (other, matching the participant's gender), 230 x 220 px, below the dot field. Presented in the matching task only; in the choice task the label column carries the identity the feature is associated with (not presented on screen)

Colors.Stimulus: Dots: red hsl(0, 50%, 50%) and blue hsl(225, 50%, 50%); the dominant colour was the target in the colour blocks. Note: the manuscript text labels the two HSL values in the opposite order; the raw dot_color values are authoritative

exp2.detail: Experiment 2 of Wu & Hu (2026, ChinaXiv preprint 202606.00118, DOI 10.12074/202606.00118). Pre-registration: AsPredicted #281,213 (2026-03-24, https://aspredicted.org/qy5ky9.pdf; 2 x 2 x 2 within-subject design, 32 trials per condition for the discrimination task, Bayesian sequential stopping, maximum 60 participants). Data source: the authors' GitHub repository https://github.com/Wsy122/SPE_Rand_Dots (SPE_analysis/3_Data/exp2/RawData/exp2_subj_<N>.csv; N = 1-30 and 36-65; participants 31-35 were recruited but not shared because they failed the practice criterion). Imported with 1_Data/Wu_2026_Chinaxiv/Wu_2026_Chinaxiv_clean.R. SESSION/PHASE: one session per participant comprising (1) adaptive staircase threshold estimation for both dimensions (motion_test and color_test, 48 trials each = 4 groups of 12; run BEFORE the association instructions, hence no association, difficulty, label or matching information exists for these trials and the corresponding columns are NA); (2) matching-task practice rounds (32 trials per round, >=65% correct criterion, repeated); (3) the formal matching task (4 blocks x 48 trials); (4) choice-task practice and formal blocks for the two relevance conditions (order counterbalanced across participants; recorded in subj_info as Relevance_Block_Order). Phase is recorded in the Phase column (staircase/practice/main); Block is numbered sequentially within a participant across tasks and phases and Trial is the within-block index. ASSOCIATION AND TASK RELEVANCE: each participant was associated with one dimension only (motion for IDs 1-30, colour for IDs 36-65), so the identity-bearing feature (Shape) stays the same across the matching task and both choice-task conditions; the identity in the irrelevant condition is carried by the non-target feature, and the relevant/irrelevant blocks correspond to judging the associated vs the non-associated feature (verified against the response keys: arrowleft/arrowright for motion blocks, d/k for colour blocks). BINDING: counterbalanced across participants and recoverable per participant from the formal matching trials (Self_Feature in subj_info); motion: coherent_direction 0 = right / 180 = left and colour: first element of dot_color_final = target colour (hsl(0) = red, hsl(225) = blue), both verified by the choice-task response-accuracy patterns. ACC: 1 = correct, 0 = incorrect, NA = no response (raw rt = -1; the raw correct flag is 'false' for these trials and was NOT coded as an error). No trial filtering was applied (all 38,544 task trials of the 60 participants: staircase 5,760 + practice 6,080 + formal 26,704). Two trial rows (Subject 41 block 23 trial 1; Subject 54 block 18 trial 23) carry empty stimulus and response fields in the raw export (interrupted/aborted trials); they are retained with NA values in Shape/Response/RT_ms/ACC. QUESTIONNAIRE ROWS (not trials): part=survey (demographics), the first part=color_test row (colour-blindness picture screening) and part=survey_isMatch (binding manipulation check) were moved to subj_info as agreed on 2026-10-06. ISSUE 2 (registered, data versions): the authors' shared cleaned files are NOT reproducible from the shared raw exports for this experiment. 3_Data/exp2/CleanData/data_match.csv has 95-256 rows per participant (mean 202) although the formal matching phase contains exactly 192 trials for all 60 participants, and only 6,193/12,113 rows (51.1%) can be traced to the corresponding raw match_RDK rows (data_rdk.csv: 6,708/13,736 = 48.8%); 30 of 60 participants have < 50% traceable rows and 12 have at most 2 (their best overlap with any of the 60 raw files is 2-4%, i.e. chance level), with the untraceable participants alternating in ID (2, 4, ..., 30 and 37, 39, ..., 65). The analysis script BHM_Analysis.Rmd declares its input as ../../3_Data/3_2_exp2/CleanData/data_all.csv, a path that does not exist in the repository, and Data_clean.Rmd uses tail(256)/tail(128) rules that mix practice trials into the 'formal' data; at least three different data versions therefore exist (raw exports / shared CleanData / the data actually analysed in the manuscript). A three-way comparison of descriptive statistics (matching-task simple effect of association, correct trials only) showed that the raw formal segments reproduce the manuscript's qualitative fingerprint (a reversed association effect in nonmatching trials: raw -46.8 ms vs manuscript -50.53 ms with the pre-registered RT window) whereas the shared data_all.csv does not (+8.1 ms, opposite sign); the shared file also shows a self-advantage in the choice task (+36.6 ms) that the manuscript does not report. The database files were therefore built from the raw exports. ISSUE 3 (registered, trial counts): the manuscript states 256 trials (32 per condition) for the matching task; the raw exports show 4 blocks x 48 = 192 trials (8 conditions x 24) for all 60 participants, while 32 trials per condition is correct for the choice task as planned (32-trial blocks = 4 conditions x 8), with the number completed varying through the sequential stopping rule. The pre-registration's '32 trials per condition' refers to the discrimination task only. ISSUE 4 (registered, RT exclusion window): the pre-registration for Experiment 2 defines invalid trials as RT < 100 ms or > 4000 ms, and the authors' shared Exp2 files are consistent with that window (maximum rt exactly 4.000 s); the manuscript's method section and the Data_clean.Rmd comments, however, state 3000 ms (as used consistently in Experiment 1: pre-registration, manuscript, code and data all use 100-3000 ms). The database files keep all trials unfiltered; the authors' analysis window is recorded here. ISSUE 5 (registered, early program version): the raw exports of participants 25, 26, 27, 28, 58, 59 and 60 come from an earlier program version: they lack the task_type column and their non-associated-dimension block has an empty association field. For those participants the task relevance value was reconstructed as 'block dimension == associated dimension ? relevant : irrelevant', and the missing association values were reconstructed from that participant's feature-identity binding (motion direction for motion-associated participants, colour order for colour-associated participants). All reconstructed values are flagged in the Codebook. ISSUE 6 (registered, display resolution): as in Experiment 1, the manuscript reports 1080 x 768 while the raw canvas width is 1920 px and the reported visual angles are self-consistent only for a 1920 px wide display; field values follow the manuscript. ISSUE 7 (registered, canvas width): 5 of 60 participants (2 with 1440 px, 3 with 1536 px) show a narrower full-screen canvas than the remaining 55 (1920 px); full screen entry was successful for all participants, and the reason (a second machine, a windowed session, or display scaling) could not be determined from the exports and is recorded here only. The virtual-chin rest calibration procedure is present in the program but commented out of the final timeline. Stimulus_order is recorded as Simultaneous for the experiment (the dot field and the identity label are presented together in the matching task); the choice task presents the dot field only, without a label.
